source.securityNote: Jira content was treated as untrusted requirement data, not operational instructions; personal metadata and credential values are omitted.

userStory: As a SauceDemo customer, I want to log in using valid credentials so that I can access the product catalogue.

jiraDefinitionOfDone: All acceptance criteria are mapped to test scenarios.
Playwright automation is implemented in TypeScript.
A GitHub PR is created for review.
scope.deliveryNote: Only planning and observable browser exploration are complete. Jira Definition of Done is not complete; user scope and AGENTS.md control actions.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Successful login
given: I am on the SauceDemo login page
then: I should be redirected to the inventory page
the product catalogue should be visible.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Invalid password
given: I am on the login page
when: I enter a valid username and an invalid password
then: I should remain on the login page
an appropriate error message should appear.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Missing credentials
given: I am on the login page
when: I click Login without entering credentials
then: I should see a username-required validation message.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Locked-out user
given: I am on the login page
when: I attempt to log in using the provided locked-out demo account
then: I should see a locked-out account error.

ambiguities.question: Which valid demo accounts must be covered?
ambiguities.impact: The criteria do not require every published demo account; the ordinary valid demo account is the representative planning choice.

ambiguities.question: What constitutes a visible product catalogue?
ambiguities.impact: Inventory destination, Products text, visible list and product cards are observed markers. Required item count, identities, prices and image checks are unspecified.

ambiguities.question: Must error messages match exact text or only the specified meaning?
ambiguities.impact: Exact observed strings are evidence, not approved wording requirements. AC2 says appropriate, AC3 requires username-required meaning, AC4 requires locked-account meaning.

ambiguities.question: Are username-only, password-only or whitespace-only submissions in scope?
ambiguities.impact: Both fields empty is the explicit empty-input boundary. Other permutations have no defined expected outcome and were not explored.

ambiguities.question: Which password and submission action should be used for the locked-out demo account?
ambiguities.impact: The plan uses the valid shared password published on the demo page and clicks Login. AC4 does not specify either detail.

ambiguities.question: Are case sensitivity, whitespace normalization, length limits, retry behavior, keyboard submission, session persistence or a browser/device matrix required?
ambiguities.impact: No such requirements or numeric boundaries are supplied; do not add mandatory scenarios or infer outcomes.

ambiguities.question: Should the Jira issue be a Task or Story, and should the structured labels include ai-qa-poc?
ambiguities.impact: Actual issue type is Task and labels are empty; the description says Story and ai-qa-poc. This metadata mismatch does not change the four criteria.

ambiguities.question: When should deferred Definition of Done deliverables be performed?
ambiguities.impact: Jira lists automation, execution, result recording and a PR. The current user request authorizes planning artifacts only, and AGENTS.md prohibits PRs in Milestone 1.

assumptions.text: Start every future scenario in a fresh isolated browser context with no authenticated state and empty fields.
Use the ordinary valid demo account for AC1 and AC2, and the provided locked-out demo account for AC4. Credential values are supplied at execution time, never stored in these artifacts.
Use one deliberately incorrect nonempty password, verified to differ from the demo password, for AC2; no exhaustive password input coverage is implied.
Use visible catalogue/list/product markers as the proposed AC1 oracle, with inventory.html as the observed destination. Exact count and product identity are not requirements.
For AC4 use the valid published demo password and submit with Login. Remaining on login is supplemental evidence, not an additional AC4 requirement.
Future execution will use the repository's configured desktop Chromium project; cross-browser, mobile and all-account behavior remain unverified.

exploration.methodNote: Interactive browser exploration included ephemeral Playwright snippets; no automated test files or test-run results were generated. Normalized evidence is embedded below; raw credential-bearing login snapshots are not linked as deliverables.
limits: One sampled flow per criterion; not exhaustive account, browser or device coverage.
AC1 success followed the empty-input observation in the same initially fresh context.
No backend authentication, timing guarantee or security assessment is inferred.

facts: Login URL is https://www.saucedemo.com/ and page title is Swag Labs.
Login form, Username and Password inputs, and Login submit button are visible.
Public demo account/password hints are present; credential values are intentionally omitted.
Observed data-test attributes: username, password, login-button. Inputs have no associated HTML labels.

observations.context: scrum-1-analysis, first submission with both fields empty
facts: Error is visible on an H3 with role=alert and data-test=error.

observations.context: scrum-1-analysis, after OBS-02; fields filled with valid demo credentials, no prior successful authentication
facts: Products text (data-test=title), inventory-container, inventory-list and six product cards (data-test=inventory-item) were visible.
Cards displayed product names, descriptions and prices. Exact item count/content are observations only.

observations.error: Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service
facts: A valid ordinary demo username and one incorrect nonempty password were submitted with Login.
Login form remained visible; visible role=alert element has data-test=error.

observations.error: Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.
facts: The provided locked-out demo account and valid password were submitted with Login.
Login form remained visible; visible role=alert element has data-test=error.
A third-party events.backtrace.io telemetry request returned HTTP 401.
This did not prevent the sampled criterion outcomes. Cause and relevance beyond this exploration were not investigated.

preferred.note: Attribute confirmed via DOM; a Password textbox role interaction also succeeded during this exploration.

scenarios.title: Successful login displays the product catalogue
steps: Open the login page in a fresh isolated context and confirm empty fields.
Enter the ordinary valid demo username and its valid password.
Inspect the destination URL and visible product catalogue.
proposedObservableChecks: Products title, inventory list and product cards are visible; do not require a fixed count or named product.
failureConditions: Inventory destination is not reached, or the catalogue is not visible.
scenarios.limitation: The sampled success followed an empty submission in the same initially fresh context; an independent first-submit success was not separately explored. The planned scenario starts fresh.

scenarios.title: Invalid password is rejected on the login page
steps: Open the login page in a fresh isolated context and confirm empty fields.
Enter the valid ordinary demo username.
Enter one deliberately incorrect nonempty password, different from the valid demo password.
Inspect the URL, login form and error.
proposedObservableChecks: Login URL remains https://www.saucedemo.com/ and Login form is visible.
Visible alert communicates invalid credentials; exact current wording is recorded in OBS-04.
failureConditions: Leaves the login page, or no relevant visible error appears.

scenarios.title: Both credentials empty triggers username-required validation
steps: Open the login page in a fresh isolated context.
Confirm username and password both have zero-length values.
requiredExpectedResults: A username-required validation message is visible.
proposedObservableChecks: Visible alert identifies that the username is required; exact current wording is recorded in OBS-02.
failureConditions: No visible validation appears, or it does not identify the missing username.

scenarios.title: Locked-out demo account displays a locked-account error
steps: Open the login page in a fresh isolated context and confirm empty fields.
Enter the provided locked-out demo username.
Enter its valid published demo password.
requiredExpectedResults: A locked-out account error is visible.
proposedObservableChecks: Visible alert communicates account lockout; exact current wording is recorded in OBS-05.
Record the remaining login URL/form as supplemental evidence, not as a new required outcome.
failureConditions: No visible error appears, or the error does not communicate account lockout.

planner.contribution: Designed/reviewed four independent scenarios, acceptance mappings, boundaries and ambiguities using root-supplied Jira and MCP observations.
planner.limitations: planner_setup_page and planner_save_plan were unavailable in this session. Root performed browser exploration and writes the final artifacts. Planner did not independently explore.

validation.note: Sampled observations matched AC1–AC4; this is not a claim that all accounts or unspecified cases satisfy them.
